Affected baseline scope: all 39 baseline items are implicated by the allergen-authority finding. Packet reconciliation counts are 39 reconciled, 39 unique, and zero duplicate keys: 37 exact_match/accurately_unavailable and 2 missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable as Terra recorded them.
Restaurant identity is verified: the official site and restaurant-linked Toast page identify Barrel and Crow at 4867 Cordell Ave, Bethesda, Maryland.

The official Food & Drink index links six image-based menu surfaces: dessert, happy hour, red wine, white wine, beer, and cocktails/spirits. The accessible page text does not enumerate their products. The site also advertises current Sunday brunch, while the available restaurant-issued brunch PDF is dated 2023.

The live Toast dinner surface contains products outside the baseline, including Gazpacho, Hanger Steak, New York, Seard Tuna Special, additional desserts, and SD Grits. New York is explicitly shown as out of stock but remains a current product presentation.
Toast duplicates featured products in their category listings, confirming presentation duplication but not duplicate products.

The PDF/image, count-drift, current-only, duplicate-presentation, low-confidence, and scout-risk gates remain substantively triggered. The aggregate current-product metrics should not be treated as an exact product inventory because Luna modeled catalogs rather than individual products.

No restaurant-issued complete allergen matrix, complete ingredient list, may-contain disclosure, or cross-contact statement was found. Therefore empty arrays cannot establish negatives, nonempty arrays cannot be treated as complete, and deterministic cross-contact counts cannot establish actual cross-contact.

Restaurant-linked Toast descriptions and restaurant-issued menu descriptions remain valid for narrow positive evidence when they explicitly name ingredients or an unavoidable item identity. Examples include fish from salmon or tuna, shellfish from crab, shrimp, crawfish, squid, mussels, or oysters, milk from Parmesan, goat cheese, Swiss, burrata, butter, sour cream, crème fraîche, or whipped cream, egg from an explicitly named egg, tree nuts from pecans, walnuts, or almonds, soy from edamame or sesame-soy glaze, and wheat only where bread, baguette, pasta, fettuccine, ravioli, or similarly explicit identities make it unavoidable.
The cross-contact gate is unresolved, not positively verified: the menus provide only a raw-or-undercooked-food warning and no shared-equipment or may-contain disclosure.

Terra's claim that Pulled Brisket Sandwich was absent from the directly opened current Toast listing is false. The reopened Toast page currently lists “Pulled Brisket Sandwich — BBQ Sauce, Coleslaw, Fries.” Only Braised Pork Shank remains absent among Terra's two claimed missing baseline products.
The reconciliation bucket of 2 missing_from_source items is not currently accurate as a live-menu conclusion; primary-source reinspection reduces the demonstrated missing baseline count to 1.
Any interpretation of the deterministic crossContactCount of 2 as source-backed cross-contact evidence is rejected.

Any blanket correction that deletes all existing positive allergens is rejected. Explicitly named ingredients and unavoidable named identities can support narrow positives, even though they cannot establish complete allergen arrays.

The PDFs themselves are not unenumerable: both reopened PDFs have extractable item text. The PDF/image gate remains confirmed because separate official menu pages are image-only and because dated PDFs do not establish a complete current catalog.
